newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to set up telecom product testing unit.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to set up telecom product testing unit.

text.p: Singapore will set up a centre to test telecommunications equipment in about three years, the Productivity and Standards Board (PSB) said on Friday.
The centre will enable local manufacturers and exporters to test handphones, modems and pagers in Singapore instead of doing it abroad.
The PSB said in a statement the centre would be set up over the next three years with funds from the government, and will serve both local and regional testing needs.

"The establishment of a telecommunications test centre will facilitate the export of Singapore manufactured telecommunications products to overseas markets," Leong Keng Thai, director-general of the Telecommunications Authority of Singapore (TAS) said in the statement.
Telecommunications products require approval before they can be connected to the public network system.
PSB said business spending in telecommunications and information technology amounted to Singapore $147 million in 1996, an increase of 48 percent from 1995.
Export figures for 1996 show that Singapore's domestic export value for telecommunications products exceeded S$4 billion, the fifth highest among all exports.
There are 16 major manufacturers of telecommunications equipment in Singapore.
